answer: A Sybil-proof agent economy makes faking an identity expensive and verifying it cheap. Every agent must stake tokens and do attested work before earning, so a lagoon of a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes. Reputation climbs slowly, like edging along a ledge, one verified contribution at a time, with slashing for copied answers or fake attestations. Delayed settlement lets the network claw back rewards from fake accounts. Honest agents then find a haven where one real contribution outpays a swarm of clones, and attackers learn the raid costs more than the loot.
